Requisition ID: REQ674241

Located in: Scott Memorial Hospital Scone

Closing Date: Sunday 12th July

About the Opportunity

Scone Hospital is seeking experienced Registered Nurses to join our Emergency Department and become part of a supportive, close-knit team delivering high-quality care to the Upper Hunter community.

Nestled in the picturesque Upper Hunter, Scone offers the charm of rural living with the amenities of a modern healthcare facility. The hospital includes a mixed medical and surgical ward, operating theatre, maternity unit, emergency department and onsite medical imaging, providing a diverse and rewarding clinical environment. Located just over three hours from Sydney, with Newcastle, Maitland, the Central Coast, Tamworth and Armidale all within easy reach, Scone offers an enviable lifestyle while allowing you to build a fulfilling nursing career. Our team is made up of experienced clinicians with a broad range of skills who are passionate about supporting one another and delivering exceptional patient care. From your first day, you'll receive a comprehensive orientation and ongoing support from our onsite Clinical Nurse Educator and Nurse Unit Manager, with access to education, transition programs and professional development opportunities to help you continue growing your emergency nursing career.

This opportunity is full-time however job share - part-time will be considered

What You Will Be Doing

As a Registered Nurse within the Emergency Department, you will deliver safe, evidence-based and person-centred care to patients presenting with a wide variety of emergency conditions.

Working within your full scope of practice and supported by Enrolled Nurses, Assistants in Nursing, Student Nurses and an onsite Clinical Nurse Educator, you will:

Perform triage assessments and prioritise patient care using recognised emergency triage principles.

Assess, plan, implement and evaluate nursing care for patients presenting to the Emergency Department.

Provide treatment, coordinate admissions, facilitate transfers and support safe patient discharge.

Respond confidently to deteriorating patients and medical emergencies.

Collaborate closely with medical officers and the multidisciplinary team to achieve positive patient outcomes.

Provide clinical support to the inpatient ward and other hospital departments during periods of lower Emergency Department activity.

Maintain accurate clinical documentation while contributing to a safe, efficient and patient-focused clinical environment.

About you

We're looking for a confident and adaptable Registered Nurse who enjoys the variety and autonomy of rural emergency nursing and is committed to delivering exceptional patient care.

Our ideal candidate will have a minimum of 12 months' post-registration clinical experience, with demonstrated experience working within an Emergency Department. You will be passionate about providing high-quality care, thrive in a fast-paced environment and enjoy working collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team.

Essential requirements:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with AHPRA.

Experience in Emergency Department nursing.

Advanced Life Support (ALS) knowledge and experience.

Experience with triage and Emergency Care Assessment and Treatment (ECAT) protocols.

The ability to effectively manage patient flow within a busy Emergency Department.

Excellent communication, clinical reasoning and decision-making skills.

A willingness to support other clinical areas within the facility when required.

A commitment to ongoing learning, professional development and delivering safe, patient-centred care.

If you're looking for a rewarding emergency nursing role where you'll enjoy broad clinical exposure, genuine team support and opportunities to continue developing your skills, we'd love to hear from you. 

What we can offer you:

 Short-term shared onsite accommodation to assist with relocation while you secure long-term housing.
 Opportunities for ongoing learning and professional development
 Sustainable Healthcare: Together towards zero
 Monthly Allocated Days Off (for full-time employees)
 4 weeks annual leave (pro-rata for part time employees)
